newsitem.title: UK: Union sees no final div, assesses future.
newsitem.headline: Union sees no final div, assesses future.

text.p: Financial services and trading group Union Plc said on Tuesday it did not expect to pay a final dividend for 1996 and was considering its future direction.
In a statement the company said the decision was related to the need to write off Advanced Corporation Tax which it had expected to carry forward.
Union also reported delays to a project to sell tax-sheltered software-related products in Canada.
Shares in Union, which had been trading close to their 12-month low before the announcement, fell 17-1/2 pence to 76 pence after the statement was issued.
Union said the Bank of England's decision, announced in December, to widen the range of participants in its money market dealings "will have a significant impact on the group's future."
It said ACT "that might otherwise have been carried forward will need to be written off," meaning that no final dividend could be paid.
"It is against this background that the board is considering the future direction of Union Plc and is examining alternative methods of releasing value for shareholders," the statement said.

Union added that plans for by two Canadian limited partnerships to raise between C$10 million and C$50 million each using software developed by its Union Fund Management (Isle of Man) Ltd subsidiary had come too late in the Canadian tax year. Offerings would therefore be made in the 1997 tax year.
"Initial indications have been encouraging but given the delay there will be no profit contribution from the Canadian offerings for Union's financial year ended Dec 31, 1996," it said.
